public_rationale: The spending threshold is checkable in principle, but the retrieved disclosures do not establish the claimed cumulative generative-AI expenditure. General capital spending and investments cannot simply be counted as money burned on generative AI. The accounting basis is also unspecified. Alphabet reports product effects, but those do not settle what Zitron means by resembling artificial intelligence.
limitations: No complete company roster or cumulative starting date is supplied.
Company claims about engagement are not independent capability measurements.
The qualitative clause cannot be resolved by substituting an evaluator-selected intelligence benchmark.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The largest tech companies have burned hundreds of billions of dollars to spread software that doesn't really do anything resembling what we think artificial intelligence looks like.

statement.excerpt: On top of the fact that the largest tech companies have burned hundreds of billions of dollars to propagate software that doesn't really do anything that resembles what we think artificial intelligence looks like
statement.document_title: The Phony Comforts of AI Optimism

from_speaker: have burned hundreds of billions of dollars
doesn't really do anything that resembles what we think artificial intelligence looks like
our_interpretation: The monetary clause describes cumulative expenditure already incurred by the post date, not announced future budgets.
The ordinary minimum for hundreds of billions is USD 200 billion.
I read burned here as spent on developing and distributing generative AI, rather than a defined accounting loss.
The cumulative starting date and company roster are unspecified. Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft and Meta are reasonable candidates, not a roster supplied by the speaker.

The capability clause invokes an unspecified conception of artificial intelligence. It cannot fairly be replaced with either a particular benchmark or a claim that the software has no useful applications.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable records establish at least USD 200 billion of cumulative expenditure attributable to generative AI by March 24, 2025. Supporting the entire sentence would additionally require an identifiable capability standard corresponding to the speaker's words.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Complete, comparable expenditure records place the aggregate below USD 200 billion, or evidence demonstrates the capabilities excluded by an identifiable standard supplied by the claim. A smaller partial total is insufficient.
